From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Emily — hi, Connor here from Solutions Engineering. Per Sergio’s note, below is the technical summary and a small export example attached. I’ll keep this high-level; happy to walk through specifics on a call.

1) Export mechanics / endpoints
- Admin API: POST /v1/admin/logs/export (start export job)
- Status: GET /v1/admin/logs/export/{job_id} (job status + download links)
- Download: presigned S3 URL (time-limited) or stream endpoint for direct ingestion

2) Formats and examples
- Supported: NDJSON (recommended for streaming), JSON array, CSV (limited columns)
- Attached sample: audit_log_export_examples.ndjson (5 events)

3) Retention and per-tenant config
- Default retention: 90 days for hosted accounts; configurable up to 7 years for enterprise contracts
- Per-tenant override: yes — retention policy can be set per-customer or per-route via the console or API

4) Immutability & tamper evidence
- Export immutability: exports can be written directly to your S3 bucket using server-side copy with object-lock (WORM) supported at upload time if your bucket is configured for object-lock.
- We provide an export manifest that includes SHA-256 hashes for each exported file and a signed manifest metadata file (signed with our service key) to support verification.
- Additionally, exported files include append-only sequence numbers and two-way hash chaining for event groups to detect missing/altered files.

5) Encryption and integrity
- In transit: TLS 1.2+
- At rest: AES-256; for S3 uploads we rely on SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS per customer config

6) Streaming vs scheduled
- Streaming: you can configure real-time forwarding of logs to a streaming endpoint (Kinesis / PubSub / direct HTTPS) with sub-second delivery for most event types.
- Scheduled bulk exports: daily or ad-hoc exports are available and will produce NDJSON bundles.

7) ACLs and auditability
- All export actions are logged in the admin activity log with requestor, IP, timestamp, and job id; these logs are also exportable.

8) Sample commands
- Start export (curl):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/logs/export -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"start":"2025-10-01T00:00:00Z","end":"2025-10-31T23:59:59Z","format":"ndjson","destination":{"type":"s3","bucket":"s3://logicorp-exports","object_lock":true}}'

9) Timeline for SOC 2 artifacts
- Neha or Lauren will share the current SOC 2 attestation/status; expected Type II report availability is Q1 2026 (we will provide compensating controls and interim evidence for procurement).

If helpful, I attached a short admin API reference (api_reference_admin_logs.md) and a small NDJSON sample. Happy to run the sandbox export for a LogiCorp test bucket. What credentials / bucket details should we use for the test?

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
